newsitem.title: SPAIN: Foreign investors fuel spurt in Madrid stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors fuel spurt in Madrid stocks.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday, encouraged by a positive international backdrop and buying by some foreign investors after a period of weakness, dealers said.
But sentiment remained wary in such choppy conditions.
The general index rose 13.30 points, 2.27 percent, to 599.86 and the Ibex-35 added 170 points, 2.56 percent, to 6,835.10.
With the Ibex having retraced to cheaper levels, the entry of final investors caused a knock-on effect.
"We were ready for a good international backdrop...then final investors --apparently foreign-- started buying big stocks, mainly banks and utilities, pulling everything up," a dealer said.
BBV rose 240 pesetas, 6.1 percent, to 4,175 in relatively heavy trade.
Endesa added 120 peseta to 3,195 and Iberdrola rose 35 pesetas to 1,850.

Repsol up 210 pesetas, 3.38 percent, to 6,420 after first half results, flat versus the year-ago period, seem to signal better things to come after poor sentiment had weighed on the stock for some time, analysts said.
